newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Vontobel, Helvetia launch first product.
newsitem.headline: Vontobel, Helvetia launch first product.

text.p: Swiss asset manager Bank J. Vontobel & Co AG and insurer Helvetia Patria Versicherungen launched their first joint product under an "allfinanz" cooperation pact.
The product, Saphir Vitafolio, is a life insurance instrument based on an investment fund managed by Vontobel and meant for sale in Switzerland.

It combines the banking and insurance business of the two partners, a merger of traditionally separate activities dubbed allfinanz that is gaining popularity among banks and insurers in Switzerland and elsewhere.
"We have the experience in asset management and Helvetia Patria has the sales channels," Vontobel chief investment officer Wolfhard Graetz.

Graetz and Helvetia Patria chief executive Erich Walser said the life insurance fund was aimed at wealthier private banking customers, a lucrative sector where both groups have been trying to win more business.
"We already have ideas for the next joint products...It is possible we will move into new customer segments or into neighbouring countries," Walser said.
Vontobel and the insurer are both medium-sized players in their markets and limited their pact, announced last February, to developing and marketing joint products.
Other bank-insurer deals in Switzerland have been forged by the biggest three Swiss banks in deals including capital swaps, jointly run businesses or both.
The big pairings are Union Bank of Switzerland with Swiss Life, including an exchange of capital, Swiss Bank Corp SBC with Zurich Insurance and Credit Suisse with Winterthur.

Helvetia Patria is active in Switzerland and Europe and had 1995 premium income of more than 3.5 billion Swiss francs. The Vontobel group managed assets of more than 24.5 billion francs by the end of 1995. -- Zurich Editorial, +41-1-631 7340
